rationale: The SwiftUI exporter binds a control, and marks it bound in its binding manifest, only when the baked C++ binder's eligibility rule (now the shared binding_route_installable: a route id, a stable anchor and the keys the widget kind reads, including a key-only meter) accepts it, so the SwiftUI, native, ui.js and C++ lanes bind the same set of controls. A refused binding reports the native binder's diagnostic code and message, and an unbound control is drawn inert on a detached parameter. The C++ plan calls the same rule, unchanged in behaviour. The emitter conformance gate's SwiftUI projection (test/test_design_emitter_conformance.cpp and its allowlist fixture, which select design-ir-contract and design-source-ingest) counts only bound manifest entries. No IR contract, Chromium, rendering or packaging authority moves.
